HEADLINE: the scripts' literal claim cannot be reconfirmed here. Seven of the nine in-scope scripts import `referencing` and `jsonschema`. Neither module is installed in any interpreter here (python3.10, 3.11, 3.12, 3.13, /usr/local/bin/python3). There are no wheels for them in /root/.cache/pip or /root/.cache/uv, and the brief forbids installing from the network. Run as-is, every one of them exits 1 with "ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'referencing'" and writes nothing.

As a clearly labelled SUBSTITUTE, I wrote a standard-library stand-in (R5/shim/referencing, about 300 lines). It implements only the parts of the `referencing` API the scripts call, following that library's documented draft 2020-12 algorithm: registry crawl and `$id` registration, lookup, pointer traversal with subresource base changes, the 2020-12 subresource keyword sets, and attrs-style exception text. `Draft202012Validator.check_schema` is replaced by Ajv 8.18.0 Ajv2020 metaschema validation (found offline at /opt/node22/lib/node_modules/serve/node_modules/ajv) plus `re.compile` of every pattern. The resources use only the 2020-12 dialect. There are no $anchor, $dynamicAnchor or $dynamicRef keywords. All 346 URIs claimed as `$id` by more than one resource map to identical contents, so crawl order cannot change a lookup. The stand-in logged 0 non-equal collisions, 0 anchor lookups and 0 other dialects.

Under the stand-in, all six v3 check scripts exit 0 with status PASS. Every count in source-review-summary.md line 15 is reproduced exactly: 1,241 original selections; 19 new roots; 1,256 literal resources; 130,201 references; 2,035 method schema positions; 240 unique roots; 1,252, 751 and 642 checks; and a 54-node, 67-edge acyclic DAG. That line reads "Deterministic checks pass: 1,241 original whole resource selections, 19 active whole roots, 1,256 literal resources, 130,201 schema-aware scoped references; 2,035 method schema positions and 240 distinct reachable method roots." STATUS.json line 11 reads `"source_consistency": "PASS",`.

Five of the six scripts regenerate their outputs byte-identically to the frozen files: composition/full-bank-checks.json, method-root-bindings.json (1,785,491 bytes, with 2,035 resolved-value SHA-256 values and per-root closure counts), method-root-checks.json, final-source-checks.json, stop-correction-checks.json and stop-phase-v3-checks.json. The stop-review v3 check.py, also under the stand-in, gives PASS; its checks.json is byte-identical and its stdout is byte-identical to the frozen check.log. It re-pins all 1,580 manifest members, confirms the exact census and the manifest hash 9ed8ba4f825939cc59b37941aafe1068be7ed2d6ada87c0e3b8eaa3b5225896e, and recomputes 130,201 references and all 2,035 resolved-value hashes. The standard-library check_delta.py gives PASS_BOUNDED_V3_SOURCE_PHASE_DELTA, with both outputs byte-identical.

So source_consistency PASS is reconfirmed CONDITIONALLY: it rests on an independent re-implementation of the resolver, not on the real library, whose version the package does not record. The byte-identical method-root-bindings.json and full-bank-checks.json are strong corroboration that the stand-in behaves like the library, but they are not proof.
